items.content: After they left she walked the rooms slowly, touching nothing, looking at how the space held the shapes of their presence — the imprint of bodies on the sofa cushions, the glasses rinsed but not yet put away, the good smell of the evening still in the air. The house was full of them, she realised. It would be full of them all night. She sat in the kitchen in the quiet and let it be.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "the particular silence of a house after everyone has left". AI text often produces grammatically perfect sentences with slightly generic emotional beats — look for overly balanced structure and lack of truly surprising word choices.

items.content: She was halfway down the block when the rain began and the smell rose from the hot pavement immediately — alive, ancestral, the smell of stone agreeing to become itself again after a long dry period of pretending to be something harder. She stopped and breathed it in. Around her, people quickened their pace. She stood still a moment longer, giving the rain its due.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "the smell of rain on hot pavement in summer". Notice the even pacing and absence of the kinds of small errors or tonal shifts that appear in prose written under genuine emotional pressure.

items.content: The tide retreated with enormous patience, taking its time about becoming less. She sat on the cold rock at the water's edge and watched it go and thought about how strange it was — that the ocean had this daily practice of diminishment and return, and that it was governed by something at a distance of two hundred and thirty-nine thousand miles, and that none of this was strange to the ocean.
items.explanation: Generated by Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 about "watching the tide go out at dusk". The polished structure and conceptually inventive metaphors are characteristic of language model output.

items.content: I write this sitting in the kitchen sink.
items.explanation: Cassandra's eccentric opening, 1948. The specificity of location (the kitchen sink, not a chair, not a desk) is a human character's self-revelation — the kind of telling detail that AI replaces with something more conventionally literary.
items.source: Dodie Smith — I Capture the Castle (1948)
